review_notes: Independently reviewed the current top-level proposal, not the different proposal embedded in the prior-result packet. The current proposal contains exactly two fact writes and no links, entities, merges, or follow-ups.

Both writes are supported: the release helper performs a single conditional addition followed by facing-dependent reflection, not general angle normalization; animation performs ordered per-invocation subtraction, mash processing, a guarded item request, and a post-call latch write.

Read both owned files completely in canonical and rendered form, all five subject pages, both link pages, the complete proposal and functionality documents, all three fact-ledger pages, both link-ledger pages, and the coverage and unresolved artifacts.

Validated foreign capture registration, item-side victim guards and cleanup, timer-controlled damage, release-sequence callbacks, common grab initialization and mash processing, position copying, the death callback, and fighter motion-table registration. The item table additionally places the relevant motion-13, motion-14 and motion-15 callbacks in entries 13 through 15 at code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/it/kinds/itlikelike.c#L35-L79. No gameplay meaning was derived solely from numeric callback names.

The functionality document accurately separates local behavior from downstream obligations. Its deferrals concerning compiled storage, literal pools, callback lifetime, damage policy, geography, and attribute ranges remain necessary. Acceptance does not promote those deferred baseline claims to proved facts.
Rendered aliases were treated only as descriptive hypotheses. In particular, Player_GetRank and collision/damage helper substitutions were not used as independent evidence.

Boundary review included zero and negative-zero comparisons, negative angles below -360, angles at or above 360, NaN/infinity, decrements that can round away, optional grab-shake processing, post-call latch ordering, caller-owned victim cleanup, and borrowed item/stack argument lifetimes.
